note: Measured, not aspirational. On 2026-08-22, after language detection was narrowed to prose (armour, data: URIs and long token runs are excised before a language is named), the shipped engine (configs/default-rules.json + the default detector registry) scored 38/39 = 97.4359% detection and 3/21 = 14.2857% false positives on this corpus. The floor is that detection rate rounded DOWN to 4dp and the ceiling that FP rate rounded UP to 4dp, so the gate cannot fail against the run that set it -- and nothing looser: one more missed malicious case takes detection to 37/39 = 94.87% (fails), one more quarantined benign case takes FP to 4/21 = 19.05% (fails). The single missed case is encoded-plus-form, recorded as a known_gap: '+'-as-space form encoding is a live bypass that PASSES at 0.70. The detection floor is deliberately NOT 1.0 -- it was briefly, and that was misleading, because a same-class bypass was passing outside the corpus. A gate that reads 100% while a known bypass ships is worse than an honest 97.44%. The FP ceiling moved down from 23.81% (5/21) when base64-image-attachment and pgp-signature stopped being quarantined; the three remaining false positives (security-advisory-quoting-injection, release-notes-with-shell, docs-act-as-proxy) are still recorded gaps in manifest.json -- they need the engine to model quotation and context, which it does not, and the ceiling exists to stop them growing, not to bless them. Move these only after measuring a real change, and say so in CHANGELOG.md. Tightening them is the point; loosening them to make a red build green is how a gate stops meaning anything.
